solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Is it paste produced in this plant?

definitions.text: Is it paste produced in this plant?

parts.words: Is it paste produced in this plant?
parts.note: paste is imitation jewellery, a fake gem; a fake is a sham and a gem is a rock, so the plant's name splits into the words for fake gem

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether a factory turns out glue or paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a factory making paste; it is the Irish clover. Paste is imitation gemstone, a SHAM ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The national emblem of Ireland is a three-leaved clover, a green herb with that name.

clue.text: Amusing person makes you laugh uproariously

definitions.meaning: to ... with laughter, shrieking loudly at a joke

explanation.surface: A comedian whose antics leave you howling with laughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally a very funny person is 'a real scream', and the verb also covers shrieking with mirth.

clue.text: Accommodation for poor soul has me troubled

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed or stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A poor soul confides that they are troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' looks like it belongs with 'soul' as the anagram signal, but it is part of the definition; 'troubled' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Charitable housing was historically built for elderly or needy people who could not pay rent.

clue.text: Studies at home, grade revised externally

definitions.note: plural noun as definition for a singular verbal noun: studying, poring over books

indicators.note: externally means the rearranged letters sit outside, wrapping round the other piece
revised means altered or reworked, so the letters of grade are rearranged

parts.note: at home means in, as in 'staying in'

explanation.surface: A student studies at home while their exam grade is revised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' looks like part of the studying picture, but it is the anagram signal, making READG; 'externally' says that wraps round the home word.
explanation.definitionFit: Academic study at university, especially of a subject, is traditionally described as perusing books.

clue.text: Traveller round sun bed the writer occupies

indicators.note: occupies means the writer's word sits inside, filling the bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the writer refers to the setter, giving me

explanation.surface: A writer lies in a bed in the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: This icy body follows an elliptical orbit about our star, trailing a tail when it nears it.

clue.text: Crone's smile entertaining lord soldiers deserted

definitions.note: read as 'Crone is', the 's being a link: crone defines the answer

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly

indicators.note: deserted means abandoned, so the soldiers leave the lord

parts.note: taken as written
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An old woman's smile as she entertains a lord whose troops have abandoned him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deserted' strips the soldiers from the lord, and 'entertaining' sets what remains inside the smile word; 'entertaining' reads as amusing but means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for an ugly old woman or hag, a synonym of crone.

clue.text: Ace quote about old times turned up in curious collection

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means the whole string is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: about means around, so the quote word goes round the next pieces

parts.note: to quote is to cite
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: An ace quotation about the old days surfaces in an odd assortment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts OX inside CITE to give CITOXE; after A, 'turned up' reverses ACITOXE.
explanation.definitionFit: Unusual, foreign or bizarre objects are grouped under this Latin-plural term for strange things.

clue.text: This writer would read up on anecdotes, hunting deity

indicators.note: read up in a down clue means this piece is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the setter would, shortened to I'd
ana is a collection of anecdotes or sayings about a person

explanation.surface: An author promises to research stories about the goddess of the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read up' turns I'D into DI. Ana means a collection of anecdotes, as in the suffix of Victoriana.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman goddess of the chase and the moon, counterpart of the Greek Artemis.

clue.text: Old-fashioned Peter out with Victor, tucking into food

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so these pieces are placed within the food word

parts.note: a meal is food
to peter out is to die away
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man called Peter goes out with a friend called Victor and they tuck into a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' looks like a man's name but 'Peter out' is the verb, dying away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hopelessly outdated is jokingly said to belong to the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Successful person a Greek character always follows

indicators.note: follows means the always word comes after the earlier pieces

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ever means always, as in 'for ever'

explanation.surface: A self-made success with a Greek follower who always shadows them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attains goals and accomplishes things is described with this noun from 'achieve'.

clue.text: Butter perhaps old farmer gives politician

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a ram
say means perhaps or for example
Old MacDonald had a farm, in the nursery song

explanation.surface: Butter, perhaps, from an old farmer is a gift to a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts: a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour's first British Prime Minister, who led governments in 1924 and 1929 to 1935.

clue.text: Who believes there is no God witnessing crime?

definitions.text: Who believes there is no God

parts.note: being at an event means witnessing it
a heist is a robbery, a crime

explanation.surface: A question about who doubts God after seeing a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who denies that any deity exists, the opposite of a theist.

clue.text: Parrot — friend keeps it on island

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the friend word contains the next piece

parts.note: mate means friend
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pet parrot kept by a friend on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to repeat or mimic someone's words, as a talking bird does, is to copy them.

clue.text: Press involved in backing outlet for novelist

indicators.note: involved in means placed inside, so the press word goes within
backing means going backwards, so the outlet word is reversed

parts.note: a vent is an outlet for air or smoke
to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: The press gets involved in backing a novelist's publication outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives TNEV, and 'involved in' puts the press word within it; 'Press' looks like the newspapers but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian author of Fathers and Sons, a nineteenth-century writer of fiction.

clue.text: Tablet to be smashed in corner

indicators.note: in means placed inside the corner word

parts.note: a nook is a corner

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A tablet device is about to be smashed in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashed' makes OTEB, and 'in' places it within the corner word; 'Tablet' suggests a pill or device, and it is both a notepad and a small computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a small portable computer and a pad of writing paper, a tablet in either sense.

clue.text: Brightest star in Norwegian band penning album

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as in a pen, so the band holds the album

parts.note: a-ha is the Norwegian pop group behind Take On Me
an LP, long-playing record, is an album

explanation.surface: The leading star in a Norwegian band writes an album.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers label the most luminous member of a constellation with the first Greek letter.

clue.text: Causing nuisance, shut up about access to field

indicators.note: about means around, so the shut-up word encloses the next piece

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut up or confined
a stile is a step allowing access over a fence into a field

explanation.surface: Someone being a nuisance is told to shut up about getting into a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoying, troublesome or pernicious, like a pest or plague.

clue.text: Gold adds interest to patronage

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
spices means adds interest or zest to, as in 'spices up'

explanation.surface: Gold makes sponsorship more attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the auspices of a body means with its sponsorship, protection or support.

clue.text: Leading by goal, change things drastically

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in 'two goals up'
an end is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A team leading by a goal makes sweeping changes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goal' looks like a football score but here it is an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something upside down, figuratively to overturn or revolutionise a situation.

clue.text: Doctor over limit on river boat

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the doctor word sits above, that is before, the next ones

parts.note: an edge is a limit or border

explanation.surface: A doctor over the limit on a river boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel that scoops mud and silt from the bed of a waterway to deepen it.

clue.text: Too brash in design, it's felt, with tassel

indicators.note: in design means arranged to a new pattern, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A designer's verdict that something is too brash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'felt' reads as the verb of feeling; it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A brimless cap like a fez, made of felt and topped with a silk tassel.

clue.text: Late deliveries expected

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries by one bowler
due means expected, as a train is due

explanation.surface: Deliveries that were expected are running late.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: Past the time it was due, such as a library book or a baby.

clue.text: Our leading lady as herself — in rubber?

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, Britain's leading lady
ER again: the Queen herself

explanation.surface: A leading actress playing herself in a rubber outfit?
explanation.walkthrough: ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is a piece of soft material used for erasing pencil marks.

clue.text: Choking smoke beginning to burn Basil?

parts.note: pother is an old word for a choking cloud of smoke or dust

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: Choking smoke as basil starts to burn in the pan.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks basil as one example of the herb family.
explanation.definitionFit: Basil is an example of a leafy plant grown for flavouring food in the kitchen.

clue.text: Food browned perfectly, seconds having been consumed

indicators.note: having been consumed means taken inside, so the seconds go within

parts.note: to a T means perfectly

explanation.surface: Food browned to perfection after second helpings were eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread grilled until crisp and golden on both sides.

clue.text: Mischievous goddess one flat-out in drawing room?

parts.note: Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin
a lier is one who lies down, flat out

explanation.surface: A mischievous goddess sprawled out in a drawing room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing room' is not a lounge but a room for drawing, an artist's studio; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's workshop or studio, literally a room where drawing is done.

clue.text: Craftsman on the fiddle a dull one

parts.note: mat means dull, without shine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A craftsman who cheats is a dull one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the fiddle' suggests fraud, but the craftsman works on violins.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cremona family of luthiers made violins in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Speech rewrite's moving result?

definitions.meaning: an address is a speech, so rewriting one is changing it; the 's reads as 'is'
moving house results in a new postal address

explanation.surface: Rewriting a speech gives a stirring result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like stirring but means relocating home.
explanation.definitionFit: When someone relocates house, the postal location they give to friends and businesses alters.

clue.text: One rolls over in sudden awakening

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
rotas are rolls or lists of names on duty

explanation.surface: Someone rolls over in bed and suddenly wakes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses IROTAS.
explanation.definitionFit: In Zen Buddhism, this is the term for a flash of enlightenment.

clue.text: Brilliant light installed in tree

indicators.note: installed in means placed inside, so the light goes within the tree

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree
a vesta is a match, something that gives a light

explanation.surface: A brilliant light fitted into a Christmas tree.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is an old word for a short match.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-rated hotels and reviews are graded excellent with the maximum rating.
